answer: In a decentralized AI consensus network, a beacon-based Sybil resistance mechanism utilizes a unique identifier, akin to an atlas of agent identities, to verify the authenticity of participating agents. By leveraging a distributed ledger that tracks agent interactions and reputation scores, an attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities on a single "island" of the network would incur significant computational costs, as their fabricated identities would require redundant verification processes, rendering the attack economically unviable.
